text:
sasha: Heads-up — ops asked for a safer way to roll out config changes that affect routing weights and quota throttles. Current feature-flag + canary flow is too coarse for per-customer quota/routing tuning. Want to propose a "gradual throttle" primitive we can expose via API + Console.

mike: +1, we've had a few incidents where a 100% weight flip killed downstream queues.

anya: can you sketch what the primitive looks like? happy to review UX.

sasha: idea sketch:

```
primitive: gradual_throttle
target: customer:acct_123
field: routing.weight
phases:
  - pct: 1
    duration: 10m
    guard: "p95_latency < 200ms AND error_rate < 0.5%"
  - pct: 5
    duration: 30m
    guard: "p95_latency < 220ms"
  - pct: 25
    duration: 1h
    guard: null
  - pct: 100
    duration: 0
```

sasha: behavior: server enforces the phase schedule, evaluates telemetry guards using the tenant's metric stream, and automatically pauses/rolls back if guards fail. You can also mark phases manual to require human confirmation.

kevin: how is this different from canary percentages? main win is built-in metric guards + pause/rollback automation, right?

sasha: exactly. Canary flow today is just percent + manual monitoring. We want a first-class object that couples percent timeline + metric predicates + audit trail.

anya: UX notes: Console should show phase timeline, live metric overlays (latency/errors/throughput), clear CTA to "pause" or "abort and rollback to N%". Also show which policy triggered an automatic pause.

devex: API shape proposal:

PATCH /api/v1/tenants/:id/gradual-throttles/:tid
body: {
  "phases": [ {"pct":1, "duration":"10m", "guard":"..."}, ... ],
  "mode": "auto|manual",
  "rollback_on": "guard_failure|sla_breach|manual"
}

devex: Response should include next_phase_eta, active_phase, last_evaluation, and last_trigger_reason.

mike: telemetry question — do we evaluate guards on aggregated infra metrics or tenant-scoped metrics? If infra, noisy tenants could mask problems.

sasha: tenant-scoped for anything that affects correctness/perf of that tenant. infra-scoped for global resource pressure (we might preempt to protect cluster SLOs).

kevin: alerting: when a guard trips and triggers an automatic pause/rollback we should emit an event to the tenant's alerting channel + write a discrete audit entry with full metric snapshot.

ops-bot: [automated] Created incident draft #INC-482 for recent routing spike. Link: https://inc.redwood/INC-482

anya: rollout UX detail — make the default conservative: small initial pct, automatic linear ramp unless user picks stepped, and an "emergency abort" that instantly sets pct back to previous stable.

sasha: we also need a dry-run mode so users can validate guards against historical windows before launching.

mike: implementation concerns: how do we store predicates? We currently have the runtime evaluation engine for alerting rules — can reuse that, but we need tenant-sanitized queries and safe execution (no heavy queries in hot path).

devex: suggest two-stage evaluation: precompute aggregates at 1m granularity, store short window in TSDB, evaluate simple predicates fast. Complex predicates get evaluated offline in dry-run.

kevin: ops question: how to revoke a running gradual_throttle when infra is under pressure? We need a cluster-level override that can cap pct for all tenants.

sasha: agreed. Add field `global_cap_pct` that can be applied by SRE. It should be orthogonal to tenant plan.

anya: console mock idea: left pane shows timeline + phases, right pane shows live metrics + short log of phase_state changes. Inline button "force abort" requires 2FA for prod tenants.

devex: security check: any config action that manipulates quotas or routing should be audit-logged with actor, ip, UI vs API, and a signed change id to support rollbacks.

mike: migration path: we should keep existing canaries working. New gradual_throttle object maps to canary if simple (single-phase). We can slowly onboard teams.

kevin: rollout plan for the primitive: 1) internal alpha for platform+SRE, 2) invite-only beta for power customers, 3) GA with docs + examples.

sasha: action items:
- devex: write API spec + example flows (sasha/anya)
- eng-platform: prototype server-side evaluator + storage for phases (mike/kevin)
- eng-runtime: integrate enforcement hook into router (kevin)
- SRE: define global_cap mechanisms + alerting hooks (kevin)
- security: ensure audit + 2FA for force actions (devex)

anya: +1 on actions. I'll mock the console screens and a short video for beta.

deploy-bot: [deploy] feature/gradual-throttle/alpha deployed to staging at 1782001256

sasha: nice — can we test a simple tenant flow on staging tomorrow? I'll add a tenant and dry-run a couple guard predicates.

mike: I'll run a load test and simulate error spikes.

kevin: one last nit — names: prefer `gradual_throttle` or `ramp_policy`? `ramp` might be friendlier in UI.

sasha: prefer `ramp_policy` for UX. We'll keep `gradual_throttle` as the internal schema name if needed.

anya: cool. wrapping up — also add doc page: "When to use ramp vs feature flag" and include checklist for metrics to guard on.

sasha: thanks everyone. We'll sync after the staging run and iterate on guard DSL.
